subject: Procurement gating & trial monetization timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Kim <laura@novum.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novum.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement gating & trial monetization timeline

Hi Laura / Tom — great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations on procurement and how/when the trial will convert to paid.

Recap (post-demo):
- Novum wants to validate a small production workload (search + embeddings) during a 30–45 day trial window.
- Primary gating items from your procurement team: PO vs card decision; vendor paperwork; invoice format + remit details.
- Success criteria we heard: average p50 latency < 150ms for embedding lookups, 95% of integration test suite passing, and sustained daily volume of ~75k tokens/day for 2 weeks.

Questions / asks for procurement path decision:
1) Do you prefer a Purchase Order (PO) or card? (we heard PO on the call but want official confirmation)
2) Any constraints on vendor name / billing address / tax IDs we should use on the quote & invoice?
3) Is marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace / GCP) a possibility later this quarter, or should we treat this as a direct vendor engagement?

Trial => paid conversion mechanics (proposed):
- Billing start triggers: Billing will begin on the earlier of (a) receipt of a signed PO effective date, or (b) 2027-06-01 if a PO is not required and the trial moves to chargeable usage.
- Usage threshold: we will not invoice unless cumulative trial usage exceeds $500 in run-rate (roughly ~75k tokens/day sustained) — aim here is to avoid small one-off charges during exploration.
- If you want the trial to remain free for the full 45 days regardless of usage, we can mark that in the SOW.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short PO checklist and our initial SOW draft for your procurement team to review. Also linking the draft quote.

Next steps (suggested):
- Laura/Tom: confirm PO vs card and preferred invoice details (billing contact + email).
- Novum procurement: review attached PO-checklist and SOW and provide any required redlines by 2027-05-25 so we can expedite.
- Redwood: we will prepare a PO-friendly invoice and an updated SOW (if needed) and share DocuSign links.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with an updated SOW by tomorrow EOD after Ben and Grace weigh in.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191

Attachment stubs: Novum-PO-Checklist.pdf (PDF), SOW_Novum_v1.docx (DOCX), Redwood-Quote-NOV-4721.pdf (PDF)

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@novum.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novum.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement gating & trial monetization timeline

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers from procurement:

- We will proceed with a PO for this engagement (preferred).
- Marketplace purchase is not an option for this fiscal procurement cycle (internal rules).
- Procurement needs the following on the quote/invoice: "Novum Analytics, Inc.", billing address (we'll pass the full address via procurement@novum.com), and our tax ID (will share separately).

Timeline note: our procurement cadence is ~10 business days from receipt of final SOW/quote. If you can issue a PO-ready quote today (with vendor details editable), we can start internal approvals and aim to have a PO by the end of May.

Also — we'll want the invoice to map to the PO number exactly when issued.

Tom
Director of Integrations
Novum Analytics

Soojin —

Looks good. A few internal notes before we send updated materials:
- I’ll produce a PO-friendly quote template that has editable vendor fields + tax lines so their procurement can paste in exact billing info.
- We should lock the trial policy in the SOW: either (A) no charges until PO effective date or (B) threshold-triggered billing once usage > $500 run-rate. I recommend option A for Novum given their procurement timeline; reduces friction.
- Grace can own the SOW redline turnaround.

I’ll attach the quote PDF and a short checklist we can send to procurement.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Finalized SOW & PO-ready quote (next steps to get to PO)

Hi Laura / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per procurement preference for a PO, attached are:
- PO-ready quote (Redwood-Quote-NOV-4721.pdf) — editable vendor fields on the cover page.
- Updated SOW (SOW_Novum_v1.docx) — highlights: 30-day standard trial, option to extend to 45 days by mutual agreement; billing only begins on PO effective date (per Novum request).
- PO checklist (Novum-PO-Checklist.pdf) with the exact fields procurement usually needs.

To keep momentum:
1) Tom / procurement: confirm the billing contact + full billing address and preferred PO number format (reply to procurement@novum.com).
2) If procurement is okay with the SOW redlines as-is, we’ll send a DocuSign SOW for signature. Link below.
3) If you prefer to keep the trial free regardless of usage for the full 45 days, confirm and we’ll mark that explicitly in the SOW.

DocuSign SOW: https://www.docusign.com/en/document/ABCDEF-4721
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4721

We’ll stand by to issue the final invoice once PO is received. If procurement can meet the end-of-May target, we should be able to start billing the first week of June based on PO effective date.

Thanks again — let me know if you want a short sync with procurement + our billing ops to walk through the PO fields.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
